dialect: Brazilian Portuguese (broadly neutral, everyday spoken standard; você as default 'you')

profile.noun_citation: bare lemma (gender noted in discussion when it is not predictable)
profile.pronunciation_convention: IPA, broad, Brazilian (São Paulo/Rio neutral); spoken = stress hint
profile.grammar_notes: Two copulas: ser (identity, origin, time) and estar (state, location right now); ficar for the location of fixed places and for 'become/stay'. Existence: impersonal 'tem' in speech (há in writing). Have: ter. Referring to people: você/vocês as the default 'you' with 3rd-person verb forms, 'a gente' as spoken 'we' with 3rd-person singular verb; tu is regional. Negation: não before the verb, double negation with nada/ninguém/nunca/nenhum. Questions: rising intonation, question words (o que, quem, onde, quando, como, por que, quanto, qual), no inversion. Modal jobs: poder (can), querer (want), precisar de (need), ter que (must), dever (should). Future in speech: ir + infinitive. Progressive: estar + gerúndio (BR). Aspect: pretérito perfeito vs imperfeito. Possessive seu is ambiguous, so dele/dela are used for 'his/her'. Preposition + article contractions (no, na, do, da, pelo). Closed sets: subject pronouns, question words, negative words, possessives, demonstratives (esse/aquele/isso/aquilo in BR speech; este/isto mostly written), place adverbs aqui/aí/ali/lá, ontem/hoje/amanhã, irregular comparatives melhor/pior/maior/menor. No grammatical politeness levels beyond você vs o senhor/a senhora.
